contracts.blurb: Nearby kiosks want fresh egg rolls and puff-puff packs every morning.
A supermarket chain stocks your frozen moi-moi in every freezer.
Hotels and party caterers order small chops trays by the thousand.
Up-country distributors carry your akara and puff-puff mix by truck.
Sealed plantain chips and snack mixes cross the border by container.
Diaspora shops abroad want frozen moi-moi that tastes like home.

belt.name: Hot Snack Conveyor
belt.blurb: Carries akara and puff-puff from the fryer straight to the counter.

auto.name: Bean Peeler & Grinder
auto.blurb: Washes, peels and grinds beans by itself. No more aching arms.

pack.name: Freeze & Seal Line
pack.blurb: Blast-freezes and seals snacks in branded packs fit for export.

milestones.title: Second Frying Pan
milestones.blurb: Your first branch opens. The recipe now has to work without you standing at the pot.

milestones.title: Five Spots in Lagos
milestones.blurb: Mainland and Island both know the name. Time to cook batter in one central kitchen.

milestones.title: Lagos Snack Chain
milestones.blurb: Ten spots share one menu, one uniform and one supply van route across the city.

milestones.title: Beyond Lagos
milestones.blurb: Ibadan, Abeokuta and Benin get branches. Regional managers start earning their pay.

milestones.title: Nationwide Name
milestones.blurb: From Port Harcourt to Kano, every motor park has your puff-puff. Bulk beans get cheaper.

milestones.title: One Hundred Fryers
milestones.blurb: A training school now teaches new cooks the akara recipe before they touch hot oil.

milestones.title: West Africa Welcome
milestones.blurb: Accra, Cotonou and Lome open. Dodo travels well and the neighbours love moi-moi.

milestones.title: Coast to Coast
milestones.blurb: From Dakar to Douala, franchise partners queue to carry the Iya Basira signboard.

milestones.title: Diaspora Doors Open
milestones.blurb: London and Houston branches open. Homesick customers cry small on the first bite.

milestones.title: World Snack Empire
milestones.blurb: Five hundred spots on three continents, all started from one roadside frying pan.

staff: Who get the next batch of puff-puff?
Abeg pass me the bean paste.
Oil don hot, make I drop dodo.
Wrap ten moi-moi for table four.
Yam don finish, I dey slice more.
Mind the hot oil, my sister.
This queue long pass third mainland!
Small pepper or plenty pepper, ma?
I go fry am fresh, two minutes.
My hand dey sweet today, I swear.
Change dey, no worry, I dey come.
customer: Give me akara, five hundred naira.
Add extra dodo for me, abeg.
Two egg rolls, I dey rush work.
Madam, your akara no get rival!
Fried yam with plenty pepper sauce.
My children say only Iya Basira.
I came from Lekki for this dodo!
Abeg wrap am well, na takeaway.
Akara and bread, breakfast is set.
I go carry moi-moi go office.
One more egg roll for the road.
manager: Fryer two, please check your oil.
Smile first, then take the order.
Oga, sales don pass yesterday own.
Well done all, lunch rush handled!
night: My clothes still smell of akara.
From one frying pan to all this.
Tomorrow I must buy more beans.
Mama would be proud of this dodo.
My feet tire, but my heart full.
Let me count today's money small.

events.name: Rainy Morning Rush
events.text: Cold rain is falling and everybody wants hot akara and puff-puff.

events.name: Beans Price Jump
events.text: Beans cost more at the market today. Each batch of akara eats your profit.

events.name: Yam Truck Delay
events.text: The yam and plantain truck is stuck on the expressway. Supplies crawl in.

events.name: Owambe Party Order
events.text: A wedding planner pays upfront for small chops trays. Sweet extra cash!

events.name: Food Blogger Visit
events.text: A famous food blogger is filming your dodo. Big spenders follow her in.

events.name: School Holiday Lull
events.text: Schools are closed and the morning egg roll crowd has stayed at home.

events.name: Festive Season Fever
events.text: Festive season is here. Customers gladly pay more for party snacks.

events.name: New Gas Burners
events.text: Fresh gas cylinders and clean burners. Oil heats fast and cooks fly.

research.claim: The owner of Nigeria's largest quick-service chicken chain opened its 200th store across Nigeria and Ghana, running several brands at different price points.
Exporting processed Nigerian food needs an NEPC exporter's certificate and a NAFDAC health certificate, and US-bound facilities must register with the FDA.
Ready-made puff-puff and moi-moi mixes are sold to the diaspora through African grocery stores in Texas and online across the US and Canada.
A frozen West African meals brand reached thousands of mainstream US grocery stores, showing diaspora frozen food can scale beyond ethnic shops.
